import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_7/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_7/test_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # columns: ['city', 'driver_count', 'type']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # columns: ['city', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']

# Join the two source tables on 'city' column (common key)
# This is an inner join because target examples show all columns combined per city and ride_id
df_merged = pd.merge(df1, df0, on='city', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['city': string, 'driver_count': integer, 'type': string, 'date': string, 'fare': float, 'ride_id': integer]
df_merged = df_merged[['city', 'driver_count', 'type', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']]

# Ensure correct dtypes according to target schema
df_merged['city'] = df_merged['city'].astype(str)
df_merged['driver_count'] = df_merged['driver_count'].astype(int)
df_merged['type'] = df_merged['type'].astype(str)
df_merged['date'] = df_merged['date'].astype(str)  # keep as string, no datetime conversion needed
df_merged['fare'] = df_merged['fare'].astype(float)
df_merged['ride_id'] = df_merged['ride_id'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file without the index column
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_7/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_merged.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
